samples.summary: The new read-only gates on the image-resize drag (and the shared `abortImageResizeDrag` teardown) have no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (readOnly || !imageResizeDrag) return` in `handleImageResizeMouseMove` (editor.ts:2491), a `readOnly` bail in the mouseup commit path, and a new `abortImageResizeDrag()` called from `undoFn`, `redoFn` and `resetAfterDocumentReplace`. I grepped packages/docs/test for `imageResizeDrag`, `abortImageResizeDrag`, `hitTestImageHandle` and `resize.*image` — the only hit is the pure overlay unit test (image-selection-overlay.test.ts); no test ever starts a drag. The new copy-integrity.test.ts covers selection clearing on undo/redo/reset but never asserts the drag was aborted, so a regression that leaves the document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners installed (commit of a size onto a stale coordinate, or a viewer resizing a read-only document) ships undetected. This matters more now because `handleImageMouseDown` no longer returns early on `readOnly`.

samples.summary: No test covers `recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` — read-only link-following on a hyperlinked image, the regression the new call exists to prevent
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` now runs in read-only and calls `textEditorRef?.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse(e)` (editor.ts:2661) specifically because it `stopImmediatePropagation()`s before `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` would have armed `readOnlyPendingLinkHref`. Nothing tests it: grep for `recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` in packages/docs/test returns nothing, editor-read-only.test.ts explicitly says "pointer/copy/link paths" are out of scope (its header comment, line 13-14), and copy-integrity.test.ts's read-only section only tests selection clearing on a miss. If the arming call is dropped or misordered, a viewer's click on a hyperlinked image silently stops navigating and no suite notices.
searchedFor: grep recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse in packages/docs/test and packages
read the read-only describe block in copy-integrity.test.ts

samples.summary: `mergeTableCells` is the one changed table API missing from the parameterised `tableOps` clear-the-image-selection table
samples.evidence: The diff adds `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` to deleteTable, insertTableRow, deleteTableRow, insertTableColumn, deleteTableColumn, mergeTableCells and splitTableCell (editor.ts:3633-3736). The `tableOps` array in copy-integrity.test.ts lists all of them except `mergeTableCells`, so that one mutation path's clear is asserted nowhere.

samples.summary: `applySpellSuggestion` and `insertPageNumber` gained a `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` call with no test
samples.evidence: editor.ts:3490 (applySpellSuggestion) and :3897 (insertPageNumber) both call the clearer, and both are described in the diff as offset-shifting mutations with no preceding keydown. Grepping packages/docs/test for `applySpellSuggestion` and `insertPageNumber` returns no matches at all, so neither clear is covered while the sibling APIs (insertTable/insertLink/insertImage/table ops) all are.

samples.summary: The find-bar's new `editor?.clearImageSelection()` calls before replaceActive/replaceAll are untested
samples.evidence: docs-find-bar.tsx adds the clear to `handleReplace` and `handleReplaceAll`, and copy-integrity.test.ts's last test only asserts the exported `clearImageSelection` API works — it does not exercise the find bar. Globbing packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/* and grepping the frontend tests for `find-bar`/`FindBar` returns no find-bar test file, so a future edit removing either call is invisible.

samples.summary: Nothing tests that a read-only DocCanvas actually passes `handles: false`; only the pure draw function is covered
samples.evidence: The new overlay test (image-selection-overlay.test.ts:75-83) calls `drawImageSelection(ctx, rect, { handles: false })` directly. The wiring under review — `new DocCanvas(canvas, readOnly)` in editor.ts:951 and `drawImageSelection(this.ctx, rect, { handles: !this.readOnly })` at doc-canvas.ts:683 — has no test; grep for `handles:` in packages/docs finds only the source line and that one unit test. A regression that forgets to thread `readOnly` through would paint drag handles a viewer cannot use and no test fails.

samples.summary: The 'block that is gone' test's `getSelectedImage()` assertion is vacuous, and its comment claims coverage for `updateSelectedImage` that does not exist
samples.evidence: The test calls `editor.selectImageAt('gone', 0)` on an editor where no image was ever selected, then asserts `editor.getSelectedImage()).toBeNull()` — true regardless, since `selectedImage` was never set; only the `not.toThrow()` is load-bearing. Its comment names `getSelectedImage` and `updateSelectedImage` as the hardened paths, but neither `findBlock` change is exercised: grep for `updateSelectedImage` across packages/docs/test returns nothing, and no test puts a live selection on a block that then disappears before calling `getSelectedImage`/`updateSelectedImage`.
searchedFor: read the 'selecting an image in a block that is gone' test

samples.summary: The null-`clipboardData` early return is only tested on the image branch, not on the text-selection branch whose behavior it changed
samples.evidence: `handleCopy`/`handleCut` now return before `preventDefault()` when `e.clipboardData` is null (text-editor.ts:1206, 1246). Previously the text path called `preventDefault()` and then no-op'd via optional chaining; for `cut` it also deleted the selection. The two new tests ('a null clipboardData leaves the copy to the browser', 'a null clipboardData cuts nothing at all') both set up an *image* selection only, so the text-selection case — the one where a cut used to destroy content that reached no clipboard — is never exercised.

samples.summary: The new `render()` in `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all is untested — the stale-overlay symptom it fixes is not asserted
samples.evidence: The diff adds `render()` after `selectedImage = null` in the catch-all specifically so a key TextEditor ignores (F5, dead key) does not leave the selection overlay painted. The corresponding test ('a non-modifier key still drops the image selection', pressing F5) asserts only `getSelectedImage()).toBeNull()`, which was already true before the render was added — nothing observes that a render occurred.
searchedFor: read the 'a non-modifier key still drops the image selection' test

samples.summary: Backspace on a selected image is only tested in read-only; the editable Backspace path is untested
samples.evidence: The 'deleting a click-selected image' describe tests `pressKey(textarea, 'Delete')` for the editable cases; `Backspace` appears only in the read-only refusal test. The handler branches on `key === 'Delete' || key === 'Backspace'` (editor.ts:2410), so the editable Backspace arm has no coverage.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere in the repo exercises the read-only link-arming path. Repo-wide grep for `recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` matches only src (text-editor.ts:1637/1683, editor.ts:2661) and two markdown design docs — no test file. The behavior's only observable effect is `window.open` in `handleMouseUp` (text-editor.ts:2005-2014), and no test under packages/docs/test references `window.open`/`noopener`/`_blank`. Only two docs tests dispatch a `mousedown` at all: copy-integrity.test.ts:1000 (the miss/"clear" branch, which never reaches the image-hit branch at editor.ts:2653-2668) and cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts:190 (unrelated). The read-only image test at copy-integrity.test.ts:420-438 selects via `editor.selectImageAt()`, bypassing `handleImageMouseDown` entirely, and asserts focus + copy payload only. editor-read-only.test.ts:10-16 explicitly defers pointer/copy/link paths to manual/browser tests, and there is no e2e/playwright directory in the repo. So removing or misordering the `textEditorRef?.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse(e)` call at editor.ts:2661 leaves every suite green while a viewer's click on a hyperlinked image silently stops navigating — a user-visible regression with no meaningful coverage. Major under the test-adequacy rubric.
